newsitem.title: USA: ARCO OKs funds for Alaska heavy oil field.
newsitem.headline: ARCO OKs funds for Alaska heavy oil field.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co said Thursday its board of directors approved the first phase of funding for its $93 million West Sak heavy oil development project in Alaska.
Initial work, slated to begin in October, will include drilling 50 wells and building associated facilities, the company said in a prepared statement.
The company said it has committed $54 million to the project so far.
The projects first phase will develop 51 million barrels of new reserves, or 26 million ARCO net, and add production of 7,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil, or 4,100 bpd ARCO net.

"We are proceeding with West Sak development because we have significantly lowered the cost of developing and operating new oil fields in Alaska," said Mike Bowlin, ARCO chairman and chief exectuive officer.
Production is expected to start before the end of the year.
Total development of the West Sak core area could require more than 500 additional wells and yield additional production of 62,000 bpd, the company said.
West Sak is a large, relatively shallow, heavy oil accumulation that overlies much of the ARCO-operated Kuparuk field, ARCO said.
Oil in place has been estimated at more than 15 billion barrels. West Sak development will make use of existing Kuparuk drill sites, common lines and processing centers.

"A successful Phase I project will mean additional West Sak drilling, making this the first step in a cautious 'pay-as-we-go' effort to complete development of the West Sak core area and the more than 400 million barrels of potential additional reserves it contains," Bowlin said.
